'''Data for Black Lives''' ('''D4BL''') is an American [[Nonprofit organization|non-profit organization]] with the mission of using data science to create concrete and measurable change in the lives of black people.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Rosenfeld|first=Maia|date=February 21, 2019|title=University event highlights complexities of data power|url=https://www.browndailyherald.com/article/2019/02/university-event-highlights-complexities-of-data-power|url-status=live|access-date=2021-12-21|website=The Brown Daily Herald|language=en-US|archive-date=2021-12-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211221205545/https://www.browndailyherald.com/article/2019/02/university-event-highlights-complexities-of-data-power}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |author-first=Zack |author-last=Quaintance  |date=2021-12-05|title=What Can Local Government Do to Avoid Inequitable Tech?|url=https://www.governing.com/community/what-can-local-government-do-to-avoid-inequitable-tech|access-date=2021-12-27|website=Governing|language=en|archive-date=2021-12-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211227223923/https://www.governing.com/community/what-can-local-government-do-to-avoid-inequitable-tech|url-status=live}}</ref> Headquartered in [[Cambridge, Massachusetts|Cambridge]], [[Massachusetts]], Data for Black Lives was founded by [[Yeshimabeit Milner]] and [[Lucas Mason-Brown]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Data For Black Lives, Inc|url=https://www.open990.org/org/821709461/data-for-black-lives-inc/|url-status=live|access-date=2021-11-17|website=Open990|archive-date=2021-11-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211117003240/https://www.open990.org/org/821709461/data-for-black-lives-inc/}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Roose|first=Kevin|date=2020-12-30|title=The 2020 Good Tech Awards|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/12/30/technology/2020-good-tech-awards.html|access-date=2021-12-21|issn=0362-4331|archive-date=2021-12-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211221205543/https://www.nytimes.com/2020/12/30/technology/2020-good-tech-awards.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|author-first    =Will Douglas |author-last= Heaven |date=July 17, 2020|title=Predictive policing algorithms are racist. They need to be dismantled.|url=https://www.technologyreview.com/2020/07/17/1005396/predictive-policing-algorithms-racist-dismantled-machine-learning-bias-criminal-justice/|url-status=live|access-date=2021-12-21|website=MIT Technology Review|language=en|archive-date=2021-12-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211220171210/https://www.technologyreview.com/2020/07/17/1005396/predictive-policing-algorithms-racist-dismantled-machine-learning-bias-criminal-justice/}}</ref><ref name=":1" /> Milner attended [[Brown University]]; having encountered discrimination towards the black community, she organized a group of scientists to combat the mistreatment of black people within data algorithms.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Yeshimabeit Milner {{!}} Ashoka {{!}} Everyone a Changemaker|url=https://www.ashoka.org/en/fellow/yeshimabeit-milner|access-date=2021-11-17|website=www.ashoka.org|language=en|archive-date=2021-11-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211117003249/https://www.ashoka.org/en/fellow/yeshimabeit-milner|url-status=live}}</ref>

== History ==
D4BL began in November 2017 as statistical research project, and expanded into working with a team of people on data analysis. The formation of D4BL was initiated&nbsp;by Yeshimabeit Milner, who witnessed racial discrimination, watching her peers suffer from [[Police brutality in the United States|police brutality]].<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Cocco|first1=Federica|last2=Smith|first2=Alan|date=July 22, 2020|title=Race and America: Why Data Matters|url=https://www.ft.com/content/156f770a-1d77-4f6b-8616-192fb58e3735|url-access=limited|access-date=2021-01-17|website=Financial Times|publisher=The Financial Times Limited|archive-date=2021-01-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210113170213/https://www.ft.com/content/156f770a-1d77-4f6b-8616-192fb58e3735|url-status=live}}</ref>&nbsp;Milner discovered through research that black children were getting suspended at a much higher rate than white children.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Yeshimabeit Milner (2021) {{!}} JFK Library|url=https://www.jfklibrary.org/events-and-awards/new-frontier-award/award-recipients/yeshimabeit-milner-2021|url-status=live|access-date=2021-11-17|website=John F. Kennedy New Frontier Awards Recipients|publisher=John F. Kennedy Presidential Library and Museum, National Archives|archive-date=2021-11-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211117004238/https://www.jfklibrary.org/events-and-awards/new-frontier-award/award-recipients/yeshimabeit-milner-2021}}</ref>&nbsp;After graduating from [[Brown University]], Milner incorporated her passion for [[data science]] into social activism.<ref name=":0" />

D4BL has regional organization chapters, including a group in [[Pittsburgh|Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania]].<ref>{{Cite news
|author-first=Lauren |author-last=Rosenblatt |newspaper= Pittsburgh Post-Gazette |date=Oct 5, 2020 |title=CMU grad student launches data platform to 'dig deeper' into why systems are failing Black residents in Pittsburgh|url=https://www.post-gazette.com/business/bop/2020/10/05/Data-Black-Lives-Pittsburgh-chapter-Alex-Jackson-Carnegie-Mellon-public-policy-social-good/stories/202009250125|access-date=2021-12-27|language=en|archive-date=2021-12-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211227223910/https://www.post-gazette.com/business/bop/2020/10/05/Data-Black-Lives-Pittsburgh-chapter-Alex-Jackson-Carnegie-Mellon-public-policy-social-good/stories/202009250125|url-status=live}}</ref> Additionally there is a community of other organizations working towards the same goals, including Data and Society, [[Algorithmic Justice League]], and the [[Distributed Artificial Intelligence Research Institute]] (DAIR).<ref>{{Cite news|last=Tiku|first=Nitasha|date=December 2, 2021|title=Google fired its star AI researcher one year ago. Now she's launching her own institute|newspaper=Washington Post|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/technology/2021/12/02/timnit-gebru-dair/|access-date=2021-12-27|archive-date=2021-12-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211202165034/https://www.washingtonpost.com/technology/2021/12/02/timnit-gebru-dair/|url-status=live}}</ref> 

Between 2019 and 2021, D4BL was awarded a grant by the [[MacArthur Foundation]] for broad operating support.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Gunther|first=Marc|date=August 25, 2020|title='Fund Us Like You Want Us to Win': Foundations are putting unprecedented billions into racial equity, but some grant makers worry that too little is going to grassroots movements.|url=https://www.philanthropy.com/article/fund-us-like-you-want-us-to-win|url-status=live|access-date=2021-12-27|website=Philanthropy.com|archive-date=2021-12-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211227223919/https://www.philanthropy.com/article/fund-us-like-you-want-us-to-win}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Data for Black Lives|url=https://www.macfound.org/grantee/data-for-black-lives-10115070/|url-status=live|access-date=2021-11-17|website=MacArthur Foundation|archive-date=2021-11-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211110010818/https://www.macfound.org/grantee/data-for-black-lives-10115070/}}</ref>
